_meta.title: TriageWiseProdrome — event logging cases (reqs 1.20, 1.20-T)
_meta.validates: That each triage action writes the correct event_log row(s): right event_type, linked intake_id/patient_id, at the right moment.
_meta.nature: INTEGRATION, not pure-function. Each case performs an action through TriageService (or the API) and asserts the event_log rows that result. There is no score/return value to check here — the assertion is on the side effect (rows written to event_log).
_meta.how_to_use: For each case: perform 'action' against a seeded state, then assert that event_log contains exactly the rows in 'expect_events' (matching event_type + that intake_id/patient_id are populated). 'order_matters' notes where sequence is asserted.
conventions: event_log has no performed_by (no auth in this system).
Every row carries event_type + intake_id + patient_id (soft FKs).
A single action may emit multiple events (e.g. submit → intake_created + score_calculated + queued).

reprioritized fires ONLY when queue order actually changes (a patient crosses another) — on new arrival, clinical update, or override. A re-score that doesn't move anyone emits no reprioritized event.
status_changed covers the whole status lifecycle (WAITING/IN_ROOM/DISPOSITIONED) — it replaced a separate 'dispositioned' event.

cases._why: A successful POST /patients is one action that emits several events: the record was created, scored, and placed in the queue.
cases._note: If the queue insert also emits 'reprioritized' on arrival, add it here — depends on whether arrival counts as a reprioritization in your impl.

cases._why: When a submitted intake trips a red flag, a red_flag_fired event must also be written.
cases._note: stroke complaint fires flag 5. Assert red_flag_fired only when at least one flag actually fired.

cases._why: Negative case — a clean intake fires no flag, so NO red_flag_fired event should be written.
If scoring fails (422), the transaction rolls back — no score_calculated or queued event should persist.
cases._note: Whole action rolls back on CannotScoreError — assert event_log gained NO rows for this intake, including intake_created if it's inside the rolled-back transaction.

cases._why: A PATCH that changes vitals re-scores AND moves the patient past another in the queue → case_updated + score_calculated + reprioritized. A filler patient is seeded ahead of the target so the update produces a real order change (reprioritized fires only on actual movement).

action.note: SpO2 90 + RR 26 fire two vital rules → target's acuity rises and it crosses the filler

cases._note: reprioritized fires because queue order actually changed (4021 moved ahead of 9001), matching the 'only on real movement' semantics.

cases._why: A clinical update on the ONLY patient in the queue re-scores but cannot change relative order, so reprioritized must NOT fire. case_updated + score_calculated still do.

action.note: HR 110 changes the score but there's no one to cross → order unchanged

cases._why: A status-only PATCH does not re-score → only status_changed, no case_updated / score_calculated.
Setting status DISPOSITIONED removes from queue and logs status_changed (the lifecycle event covers disposition).
cases._note: No separate 'dispositioned' event — status_changed covers it. Queue removal is a side effect, not its own event unless you emit reprioritized for the shift.

cases._why: A clinician override records override_applied and can change ordering → reprioritized.
cases._note: reprioritized only if the override actually changes queue position; if your impl always re-queues on override, it always fires.
Confirm whether black-box mode also logs this, or only xai. Adjust if they differ.

cases._why: Structural invariant across all logged rows: event_type non-null, intake_id + patient_id populated, no performed_by column.
